1	# Sideagent nodes, results and Host continuity
2	
3	`S` is the `state` command of [lifecycle-state.md](lifecycle-state.md);
4	`execute` and `collect` are in [dispatch-collect.md](dispatch-collect.md).
5	
6	## Implementation items
7	
8	`scope: implementation` is the only scope that admits `mutation: true`.
9	`execute` claims nothing, makes no worktree and touches no forge: the worker's
10	Workflow owns that. Each item sends either its own `prompt` exactly, or the
11	plan's `core` (with `core_revision`) plus the item's `worker_scope`, joined by
12	one blank line; never both. The index row's `prompt_source` keeps the kind,
13	core revision and `sha256:` of core, scope and sent prompt.
14	
15	With `--state FILE`, an item's `task_id` adds its id to that task's
16	`dispatch` (writer `tool:execute`, no Host revision); an unknown task is
17	`evidence.task_note`. A hold naming the item's `preset` (or `presets`) makes
18	it `not-run` / `on-hold` before any Runner call: a known hold is not probed
19	again. An exactly reconciled prior item stays reconciled.
20	
21	## Results
22	
23	A `collect` result has `excerpt` (480 characters) with `excerpt_truncated`
24	and `reply_chars`; `turn` (holder, prompt fingerprint); `locator` (the Runner
25	`capture` argv `--since <dispatch cursor> --full --inline` and the event log);
26	`output` with its `kind`: `file` (a path, or `{"path": ...}`; checked for
27	presence), `capture` (the reply itself), `remote` (a URL) or `description`
28	(text with spaces); an explicit `{"kind": ...}` wins; and `gaps`:
29	`reply-text-absent`, `capture-truncated`, `output-absent` (a file only). A gap is evidence,
30	not a transport failure. Read the full reply through `locator` before a
31	verdict. A new return resets `acceptance` to `pending` and keeps the earlier
32	value as `prior_acceptance`.
33	
34	## Per-assignment dispositions
35	
36	Task `dispositions` maps item id to `accepted`, `repair`, `cancelled`,
37	`superseded` or `handed-off`. It is Host-owned like `verdict`, which stays the
38	task-level judgment. `$S update --kind tasks ... --index I` mirrors them to the
39	index `acceptance` with `acceptance_source`. After a task verdict, an item of
40	that task without a disposition becomes `undecided` with a note, never left
41	`pending`. A mirror error is reported; the state write stands.
42	
43	## Host revision
44	
45	Each Host business write raises the file's `host_revision` and stamps the
46	record. Tool and Sideagent writes raise nothing and stamp `writer_holder`. The
47	Sideagent view lists `pending_host_changes`: `host:<kind>/<id>@<rev>`,
48	`host:section/<name>@<rev>` and `host:retired/<kind>/<id>@<rev>`.
49	
50	## Node mode
51	
52	Bind `--section sideagent` with `"mode": "node"` and
53	`"recipe": {"runner": "<absolute Runner file>", "argv": ["start", "--repo",
54	"<root>", "--session", "<bound name>", "--role", "sideagent", ...]}` (the
55	checkout `kaola-tmux.sh` takes the platform before `start`), without
56	`--continue` or `--resume` (an optional absolute `state_tool` names
57	`kaola-dispatch.py` when it is not beside the holder or in the sibling Skill). Worker
58	returns and terminations are not node inputs: they reach the Host at its next
59	idle boundary as without a binding, and the Host reads the original. A Host
60	holder advertising `sideagent-node/1` starts a node only for Host business
61	changes past the handled revision, selected when the Host turn has ended, so
62	one turn's writes are one batch. It starts one fresh node from that argv (no
63	shell), sends one prompt with the batch id, the Host revision range and the
64	node's role limits (source pointers only, no restated result, no dispatch or
65	judgment, exact-stop only a Host-recorded reclaim), and reads the node's checkpoint at its turn end. A turn end alone
66	acknowledges nothing. A refused recipe is logged once.
67	
68	The node writes once:
69	
70	```bash
71	$S checkpoint --writer sideagent --source B --batch B --through-host-revision R \
72	  --entries '[{"input":"<id>","applied":["tasks/t1"]},{"input":"<id>","retained":"tasks/t2"}]'
73	```
74	
75	`applied` names current records, or `retired:<kind>/<id>`, that this node's
76	holder wrote. `retained` names a current record with `next`, `owner` or `wait`,
77	or a Host `section/<name>`. Older or foreign evidence settles nothing. The
78	result is `maintenance.last_checkpoint`; `last_verified` moves only when every
79	input settled. `acked_host_revision` never passes an unsettled change; a later
80	Host write stays pending. An input the Host rewrote during the batch is
81	`superseded`: its rewrite is the next batch's input. Unsettled inputs go to the Host once, in one
82	`maintenance-returned` alert, and are never sent to another node.
83	
84	After a verified batch the carrier wakes the Host once, at its next idle
85	boundary, only when an attention item is a record this node wrote and the
86	Host view's attention differs both from what the Host last saw and from the
87	batch's start; otherwise it stays quiet. A partial or
88	missing checkpoint, one whose `through` is below the batch's range, a refused
89	batch, a failed start or a lost node reaches the Host once with the unhandled
90	range; the carrier then exact-stops the node by holder and starts no node for
91	that range again. A failed start or refused batch starts no further node until
92	the binding changes. After `sideagent_node_stop_unconfirmed` no node starts
93	while that holder process still runs. A Host stop in any mode also stops its
94	own node, a start in flight included. A replaced node's late write is
95	`binding-superseded`. There is no timer: the next Host change starts the next
96	node at a Host turn end or the existing idle tick.
97	
98	## Host continuity stop
99	
100	`stop` or `drain-restart` with `--preserve-dispatched-workers` on a Host whose
101	holder advertises `preserve-dispatched/1` keeps each worker tree that Host
102	dispatched (spawn line or a worker record naming its holder) on a cooperative
103	or dead-holder stop; other children are still swept. An older live holder
104	refuses with `preserve-unsupported` and stops nothing: `drain-restart` it at
105	idle first. The successor then runs each seat's `rebind-host`. A start still in
106	flight is not covered: reconcile it. Default stop and final close-out are
107	unchanged; close-out reclaims workers one by one first.
108	
109	## Idle wake
110	
111	A worker's undelivered `idle` wake to its Host is kept like a permission wake
112	and re-sent when the Host is reachable; a newer one replaces it and a stop
113	drops it.
114	
115	Shown live: fresh nodes on Codex and ZCode, worker survival through a Host
116	preserve stop and rebind on both, and a model-driven Codex Host with a Codex
117	node binding.
118	Not shown live: node mode on the other runtimes.

1	# Lifecycle state
2	
3	`<project>/.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json` schema `kaola-heartbeat-prompt/2`
4	holds current tasks, the adopted authorization projection, the Sideagent
5	binding, holds, alerts and pending decisions. Its `body` is the generated Host
6	view, not a second source. Change it only through `state` in
7	`scripts/kaola-dispatch.py`; a hand edit skips revision checks. The Delegator
8	file, dispatch index, Runner receipts, Git, forge and Workflow keep their own
9	facts; state keeps references, current conclusions and next steps, never a
10	copied backlog, ledger or history.
11	
12	## Roles
13	
14	- Host: goal, task split, needed abilities, dependencies, preset choice,
15	  assignment text, `execute`/`collect`, reading original results, acceptance
16	  and closeout decisions; bootstrap, failure and urgent recovery. It may read,
17	  search, analyze and do simple authorized work itself.
18	- Tools record dispatch, result and holder facts; no node restates them.
19	- Sideagent: one maintenance role per project, outside every Class seat; a
20	  fresh node per meaningful batch. It reconciles duties, holds, alerts,
21	  conflicts and reclaim, and exact-stops finished workers. It assigns, grants
22	  and accepts nothing. Launches use bypass permissions; a residual prompt is an
23	  exception, and anything needing the user stays a pending `decisions` record.
24	- Research, QA or implementation helpers are counted, authorized items.
25	- Workers never write state (`writer-refused`).
26	
27	No synchronous Sideagent round trip or approval stage per action: coalesce
28	related updates and reuse valid evidence. The Host gets outcomes, capacity and
29	pending decisions; evidence stays by reference.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	`S="python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/kaola-dispatch.py state"`. Every write takes
34	`--file "$PROJECT/.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json" --writer host|sideagent
35	--source "<event, receipt or Host turn>"`.
36	
37	- `$S init [--project JSON] [--authorization JSON]`: Host only; refuses an
38	  existing file (migrate it).
39	- `$S update --kind tasks|holds|alerts|decisions --id ID --set PATCH
40	  [--expect-rev N]`: JSON merge patch of one record (`null` deletes a key;
41	  `@path` reads a file). An existing record needs `--expect-rev`; a stale one
42	  exits 3 with `current` and `unapplied`: merge by evidence and retry, never
43	  rewrite the file. `--coalesce` counts a repeated alert.
44	- `$S update --section project|authorization|sideagent|recovery|unverified
45	  --expect-revision N --set PATCH`: first three Host-only.
46	- `$S retire --kind K --id ID --expect-rev N --evidence REF [--outcome T]
47	  [--index I --live L] [--handoff TASK]`: a task needs verdict `accepted` or
48	  `cancelled`, its dispatch items closed and seats stopped, or handed to a
49	  continuing `TASK`.
50	- `$S view --role host|sideagent|delegator [--repo ROOT]` (read-only).
51	- `$S checkpoint`, `update --index`: [sideagent-node.md](sideagent-node.md).
52	- `$S check [--index I] [--live L] [--repo R]`: read-only problems such as
53	  `doing-untraced`, `done-not-retired`, `transcription-unechoed`,
54	  `sideagent-not-live`, `carrier-unproven`.
55	- `$S migrate [--index I] [--live L] [--repo R] [--write]`; `$S timer`
56	  is the Delegator's.
57	
58	## Records
59	
60	- `tasks` (stable id; `stage` `todo|doing|review|closeout|done`, `goal`):
61	  `source`, `scope`, `needs`, `depends`, `acceptance`, `keep_open`, `wait`,
62	  `dispatch` (index item ids), `evidence`, `next`, `verdict`, `dispositions`
63	  (per item). A repair keeps the task id; one returned branch is not
64	  completion. A task needs no issue; Workflow owners keep claim/ledger/finalize.
65	- `holds` (`scope`, `reason`): `evidence`, `impact`, `owner`, `resume_when`,
66	  `next`. A hold keeps the grant; no takeover or quota reset lifts it.
67	- `alerts` (`level` `watch|warn|severe`, `summary`): level by evidence and
68	  impact, never by elapsed time. Read, acknowledged or in progress is not
69	  resolved; a warning blocks no unrelated work.
70	- `decisions` (`owner` `host|delegator|user`, `question`): kept until
71	  `status: settled` with evidence (Sideagent: with `--host-turn`); a
72	  notification clears no duty.
73	
74	Authorization, occupancy, task stage and service availability stay separate
75	facts. A stopped process deletes no task.
76	
77	## Touchpoints
78	
79	Update at existing events only: dispatch (task `doing`; plan items carry
80	`task_id`, `output`, optional `requires`), result and verdict, a material
81	goal, grant or fault change, recovery or adoption, and closeout. The inquiry
82	and `check` catch omissions.
83	
84	## Host verdicts
85	
86	`verdict.value` (`accepted|partial|repair|cancelled`) and the Host-owned task
87	fields (`goal`, `scope`, `acceptance`, `needs`, `depends`, `source`,
88	`keep_open`) are Host decisions. The Sideagent records one only with
89	`--host-turn <the Host turn it copies>`; the next Host view lists it under
90	`attention` until the Host writes that task. The Host corrects a wrong
91	transcription with its own `update` (also the bootstrap and degraded path).
92	Partial acceptance keeps the unfinished scope open; moving a `repair` or
93	`partial` task back to `review` keeps that verdict as `prior_verdict` and asks
94	again. A task at `closeout` or `done` without `accepted`, `partial` or
95	`cancelled` stays under `attention` (`verdict-missing`).
96	
97	## Sideagent binding
98	
99	The Host starts the Sideagent, then sets `--section sideagent`
100	`{"platform","session","preset","state":"active"}`; the started Sideagent may
101	add its own `holder_instance_id` once. A reply ending is not the duty's end. To
102	replace, the Host marks `replacing` or `failed`, starts a successor under a new
103	name and binds it; the successor continues from state, index and receipts and
104	replays no admitted work. A Sideagent stop spares each worker it dispatched
105	(spawn line or its record's `dispatcher`); a superseded seat's late write is
106	`binding-superseded`. The Host, not a failed Sideagent, repairs its record and
107	holds it. If both fail, the Delegator recovers the Host first.
108	
109	## Events
110	
111	`execute` records the real dispatcher (`KAOLA_ACP_DISPATCHER`) apart from the
112	notify target. Workers the bound Sideagent starts report to its live Host
113	holder (`sideagent-host`). A Host holder advertising `sideagent-relay/1` relays
114	them to the live bound Sideagent, which confirms at turn end and wakes the Host
115	only when attention changed; a busy Sideagent keeps them; a dead one, or a
116	failed or cancelled Sideagent turn, returns them to the Host. Delivery is
117	at-least-once, a wake hint: rebuild from index and receipts. `"mode": "node"`
118	keeps events with the Host; a node takes a turn's Host changes ([sideagent-node.md](sideagent-node.md)).
119	After a Host replacement (`--preserve-dispatched-workers`), the new Host runs
120	the seat's `rebind-host` from its own session: only that seat's carrier moves;
121	the worker runs on, its `dispatcher` still the old Host. Each seat (Sideagent
122	too) needs its own call; events staged in a dead Host need adoption.
123	`unknown-op`: `drain-restart` the seat at idle.
124	
125	## Size
126	
127	Repeats update the same id. A retired record leaves a capped tombstone; a late
128	event gets `record-retired`. Never drop an open duty to fit. The Host view is
129	bounded at 64 KiB (`host-view-too-large`). The file may reach 1 MiB only with a
130	recorded `carrier` advertising `heartbeat-state/2`, else 64 KiB
131	(`carrier-limit`).
132	
133	## Migration
134	
135	After a Skill update, at a safe point, run `$S migrate --index I --live L`;
136	without `--write` it only plans. With `--write`, each v1 `active` row becomes
137	a `doing` task with its assignment and fields kept, `pending` keeps its stated
138	stage or stays `todo`, `recovery` and the v1 host are kept, a pending row's
139	unknown keys stay inert under `legacy`, and other unknown keys, unassociated
140	index rows and an unproven Sideagent binding become `unverified`. The live
141	Host holder's features become `carrier`. The raw v1 file is kept once as
142	`heartbeat-prompt.v1-<sha12>.json`; a different copy alerts
143	`state-overwritten`. An unknown schema is refused. A repeat reports `current`
144	and still records an upgraded carrier. Migration resets no task, replays no
145	dispatch, re-plans nothing, re-asks no confirmed requirement, restarts no
146	healthy session, grants nothing.
147	
148	Live on Codex and ZCode only: preserve stop, `rebind-host`. Unproven: relay
149	across holder death, timer read-back, real state size.
